findings:

=== 1. RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate — full body (Helpers/RecruitmentHelper.cs:41-85) ===

Signature: public static EmployeeInstance GenerateCandidate(string skillName, float skillValue, Address assignedAddress, List<string> demands = null, float secondSkillValue = 0f)

Body, step by step:
  1. (line 43-50) THE SKILL SWITCH — a C# switch expression on skillName:
        "ba:skill_logisticsmanager" => new LogisticsManager()
        "ba:skill_hrmanager"        => new HRManager()
        "ba:skill_headhunter"       => new Headhunter()
        "ba:skill_pricingmanager"   => new PricingManager()
        _                           => new EmployeeInstance()
     DEFAULT branch for an unknown (or any other, incl. ba:skill_purchasingagent, ba:skill_customerservice, all retail skills): plain `new EmployeeInstance()`. NO throw, NO log, NO warning. Only those 4 HQ-manager skills get a typed subclass; every other vanilla skill is already a base EmployeeInstance here, so a custom skill is treated exactly like customerservice/purchasingagent at this line.
  2. (51) employeeInstance.Initialize()
  3. (52-54) random gender + unique name into characterData
  4. (55-58) candidateInfo = new CandidateInfo { hoursUntilExpiring = 168 }
  5. (59) assignedAddress = assignedAddress (the businessAddress passed by the campaign; null for headhunter)
  6. (60-64) characterData.skills.Add(new Skill { name = skillName, value = skillValue })  — the PRIMARY skill is put on the employee's own list
  7. (65-73) SkillData data = SkillHelper.GetData(skillName);  then  if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(data.secondarySkill)) { skills.Add(new Skill{ name = data.secondarySkill, value = secondSkillValue>0 ? secondSkillValue : GetRandomSecondarySkillInitialValue }); }
     *** UNGUARDED. `data` is the SkillData for the PRIMARY skillName (not secondSkill). SkillHelper.GetData returns Skills.GetValueOrDefault(name) => null for an unregistered skill => `data.secondarySkill` throws NullReferenceException. This is NPE site #1 and it fires for EVERY custom-skill candidate. The `secondSkillValue` float param is only consulted if data.secondarySkill is non-empty.
  8. (74-76) demands = demands ?? new List<string>(); GenerateDemands(); satisfaction = demands.Count==0 ? 100 : 50
     *** GenerateDemands() -> EmployeeInstance.GetTargetDemandsAmount() (Entities/EmployeeInstance.cs:706-714) -> JobDemandHelper.GetIdealNumberOfDemands(GetPrimarySkill(), sumOfSkillValues) -> (Entities.Employee.JobDemands/JobDemandHelper.cs:122-124) `if (!SkillHelper.GetData(primarySkill).HasTag(TagRef.Skilltag.canhavejobdemands))` — UNGUARDED, NPE site #2. Also EmployeeInstance.AddHoursPerWeekDemands (:633-652) -> JobDemandHelper.GetRandomHoursPerWeekDemandForSkill (:140-143) `SkillData data = SkillHelper.GetData(skillName); if (!data.HasTag(...))` — UNGUARDED, NPE site #3.
  9. (77) characterData.ageInDays = random 18-65y
 10. (78) hourlyWage = EmployeeHelper.CalculateHourlyWageForSkill(characterData.skills.First())
     *** CalculateHourlyWageForSkill(Skill) (Helpers/EmployeeHelper.cs:351-357) does `float baseHourlyWage = SkillHelper.GetData(skill).baseHourlyWage;` — UNGUARDED, NPE site #4.
 11. (79) initialCombinedSkillAmount = sum of skill.value
 12. (80) SaveGameManager.Current.CandidateEmployeeInstances.Add(employeeInstance)
 13. (81) EmployeeHelper.EmployeeInstancesDictionary.Add(id, employeeInstance)
 14. (82) smartphone MyEmployees badge++
 15. (83) GameEvent.Invoke("ba:gameevent_candidatereceived")

Net: GenerateCandidate hits SkillHelper.GetData(skillName) UNGUARDED at least 4 times (directly + via GenerateDemands + via wage calc). An unknown skill => NullReferenceException cascade, candidate never created. GetData itself does NOT throw (returns null); the callers deref it.

=== 2. EmployeeHelper.CreateAIEmployeeInstance(string primarySkillName) (Helpers/EmployeeHelper.cs:509-527) ===

Returns `new EmployeeInstance { characterData = new CharacterData { skills = { new Skill { name = primarySkillName, value = 50f } }, gender = random }, satisfaction = 100f }`.
  - NO switch — ALWAYS a base EmployeeInstance regardless of skill.
  - NO SkillHelper.GetData call anywhere. Completely safe with an unknown skill.
  - BUT it is NOT part of player recruitment. Only callers: EmployeeStationController.GetAIEmployeeInstance ("ba:skill_customerservice"), CleaningStationController ("ba:skill_cleaning"), Controllers/DJBoothController ("ba:skill_dj"), Controllers/SecurityGuardLockerController ("ba:skill_securityguard"), Controllers/FitnessPlanningBoardController ("ba:skill_gymtrainer"). These fabricate throwaway "AI employees" to visually staff AI/rival businesses. Not added to SaveGameManager.Current.EmployeeInstances, no wage, no My Employees entry, no HQ plan. Irrelevant as a hiring mechanism for the mod.

=== 3. How the Recruitment Agency lists recruitable skills — NOT SkillHelper-driven ===

Class UI.Dialog.RecruitmentSettings (UI.Dialog/RecruitmentSettings.cs). This is the InputTemplate DialogEntry.InputTemplateName.RecruitmentSettings shown by Dialogs/RecruitmentAgencyDialog.CandidateProperties (:66-77).

  - OnEnable (:57-80): `_availableSkills = ((RecruitmentAgencySettings)building.SpecialService.settings).availableEmployeeSkills;`
    RecruitmentAgencySettings (Buildings/RecruitmentAgencySettings.cs) is just `public class RecruitmentAgencySettings : SpecialServiceSettings { public string[] availableEmployeeSkills; }` — a [CreateAssetMenu] ScriptableObject attached to each recruitment-agency Building asset, loaded via Addressables. HARD DATA, not a runtime list.
    The skills dropdown is first filled from `_availableSkills` but immediately disabled (SetInteractable(false)) until a business is chosen.
  - SelectBusiness(int) (:96-120): `businessSkills = BusinessTypeHelper.GetData(selectedBusiness).employeePrimarySkills.Intersect(_availableSkills).ToList();` (+ a hard-coded special case: adds "ba:skill_cleaning" if the agency allows it and BuildingTypeHelper.GetData(...).NeedsCleaning). Then `skillsDropdown.SetOptions(businessSkills)`.
    => The recruitable set for a given business = (that BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills) ∩ (that agency's RecruitmentAgencySettings.availableEmployeeSkills). Both operands are addressable ScriptableObject string arrays.
  - SelectSkill(int) (:122-134): sets selectedSkill; then `if (SkillHelper.GetData(selectedSkill).HasTag(TagRef.Skilltag.hashoursperweekdemand))` — UNGUARDED NPE if the chosen skill is not in SkillHelper.
  - Dialogs/RecruitmentAgencyDialog.OnRecruitmentSettingsSet (:145-232, line 158): `SkillHelper.GetData(inputTransform.selectedSkill).HasTag(TagRef.Skilltag.hashoursperweekdemand)` — UNGUARDED again. Then builds `new RecruitmentCampaign { skillRequirement = new SkillRequirement { skillName = selectedSkill, percentage = 20f }, ... }`, charges money via GameManager.ChangeMoneySafe, adds to SaveGameManager.Current.RecruitmentCampaigns.
  - Campaign runtime: Entities/RecruitmentCampaign.CheckForCandidates (:58-72) -> `RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate(skillRequirement.skillName, Random(20f,50f), businessAddress, GetCandidateDemands())` on scheduled hours; sets candidateInfo.sourceAddress. RecruitmentHelper.RunHourly (:28-39) drives all campaigns each hour.
  - Agency gating (RecruitmentAgencyDialog ctor :18-42): requires a completed DiplomaName.BasicHr, and >=1 rented BuildingRegistration with a non-blank BusinessName.

  CAN A MOD ADD TO IT BY JUST REGISTERING THE SKILL? NO. SkillHelper is never consulted to build the agency dropdown. A SkillHelper-only registration leaves the custom skill invisible in the agency. To surface it a mod must EITHER:
    (a) append the skill name to `RecruitmentAgencySettings.availableEmployeeSkills` on every recruitment-agency building asset AND to the target `BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills` (both are loaded ScriptableObjects — mutate them after load via Harmony postfix on the addressable callbacks / BusinessTypeHelper.OnBusinessTypesLoaded, or reflection), OR
    (b) Harmony-patch RecruitmentSettings.OnEnable / SelectBusiness / SelectSkill to inject the skill into _availableSkills + businessSkills and keep selectedSkill valid.
  Because SelectBusiness rebuilds the dropdown as the intersection with employeePrimarySkills, option (a) still requires the BusinessType side no matter what — patching only availableEmployeeSkills is not enough.

=== 4. EmployeeHelper.HireCandidate(EmployeeInstance) — every side effect (Helpers/EmployeeHelper.cs:529-549) ===

  1. (531-535) if GetEmployeeInstances().Contains(candidate): Debug.LogWarning("Ignored duplicate hire...") + return.
  2. (536) SaveGameManager.Current.CandidateEmployeeInstances.Remove(candidate)
  3. (537) EmployeeInstancesDictionary.TryAdd(candidate.id, candidate)
  4. (538) FinishPendingNegotiation(candidate, accepted:true) -> (:560-568) finds SaveGameManager.Current.candidateSalaryNegotiations matching this candidate and sets .accepted=true/.completed=true
  5. (539) SaveGameManager.Current.EmployeeInstances.Add(candidate)
  6. (540-541) smartphoneUI MyEmployees badge + fullMenu.myEmployees.UpdateBadge()
  7. (542) candidate.candidateInfo = null   (stops being a candidate)
  8. (543) candidate.dayHired = SaveGameManager.Current.Day
  9. (544) candidate.nextSickDay = GetNextSickDay(candidate)  (pure math on satisfaction + Day)
 10. (545) candidate.AddTodoTask(candidate.IsAssignedToAnyBusiness() ? EmployeeIdle : EmployeeUnassigned, invokeQuestAffectingChange:false)
 11. (546) candidate.complaintData.ResetHoursUntilNextComplaint()
 12. (547) GameEvent.Invoke("ba:gameevent_employeehired")
 13. (548) HappinessHelper.AddModifier("ba:happinessmodifier_first_employee")

  NO SkillHelper.GetData anywhere in HireCandidate or its direct callees. Hiring is skill-agnostic — wage/skills/demands were all frozen at GenerateCandidate time. So once a candidate object EXISTS, hiring it works for any skill string.
  Callers: CandidateCellView.Hire() (CandidateCellView.cs:205-214), UI.Smartphone.Apps.MyEmployees.Types/HireCandidateMassAction, .../AssignToBusinessAndHireMassAction.
  Candidate card render path is also safe: UI.Smartphone.Apps.MyEmployees/CandidateModel ctor (:34-42) uses instance.GetPrimarySkill() (EmployeeInstance.cs:238-241 = characterData.skills.First().name) and instance.GetSkillValue(primary) (:243-246 -> GetSkill (:280-291) walks the employee's own skill list, Debug.LogWarning + null only on a genuine miss — primary is present, so fine). Neither touches SkillHelper. CandidateCellView.SetData / IsValidBuildingRegistration use BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills + EmployeeInstance.HasSkill (silent) — no SkillHelper.GetData. The "assign to business" dropdown on the candidate card will only offer businesses whose BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills contains the custom skill (CandidateCellView.cs:175-182), another reason the BusinessType asset must list it.

=== 6. Realistic answer: does recruiting "just work" once the skill is in SkillHelper + GetData guarded? ===

  - Through the vanilla RECRUITMENT AGENCY: NO. A UI/asset patch is also required. The agency dropdown = BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills ∩ RecruitmentAgencySettings.availableEmployeeSkills; neither is derived from SkillHelper. You must add the skill name to those ScriptableObject arrays (Harmony postfix on the addressable load callbacks / BusinessTypeHelper.OnBusinessTypesLoaded / reflection) or Harmony-patch RecruitmentSettings.OnEnable+SelectBusiness+SelectSkill. The candidate-card "assign to business" dropdown and CandidateCellView.IsValidBuildingRegistration also key off BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills, so the BusinessType side is unavoidable.
  - Through the HQ HEADHUNTER: the skill LISTING "just works" (SetUpSkillsToRecruitArray reads SkillHelper.AllSkillNames). But you still must (a) register the SkillData with sane fields, (b) guard/populate the still-unguarded GetData derefs in HeadhunterPlan.GetWageRangeForSkill / CheckForRecruiting / GetRandomDemandsForCandidate, and (c) have the player own an HQ + a hired headhunter.

  MINIMUM to make the vanilla agency recruit a custom "Filiaalmanager" / "Team Leader":
    1. Build a SkillData at runtime (ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<SkillData>, BigAmbitions.Characters.Skills.SkillData : TaggedScriptableObject) and insert it into the private static Dictionary<string,SkillData> SkillHelper.Skills (reflection, or Harmony postfix on SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded). Re-inject on EVERY save load: AddressableLoader.RegisterAndLoadAll() (called from SaveGameManager.TryPrepareLoad:339 and new-game:466) does Skills.Clear() then repopulates from the "Skills" addressable label only. Set: skillName, baseHourlyWage (~30 for Store Manager / ~20-24 Team Leader), secondarySkill = "" (empty — avoids the secondary-skill branch entirely), trainingCostMultiplier, icon28 sprite, possibleDealbreakers = new List<string>() (empty is fine, GetDealBreakersForSkill is guarded), and the tag list. After setting tags call BuildTagCache() on it (AddressableLoader does this automatically for loaded assets; a hand-made one needs it manually). Relevant tags referenced on the recruit path: TagRef.Skilltag.canhavejobdemands, TagRef.Skilltag.hashoursperweekdemand, TagRef.Skilltag.forcefulltime.
    2. Add a Harmony null-guard (or ensure registration happens before any recruit) on the unguarded callers: RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate:65, EmployeeHelper.CalculateHourlyWageForSkill(Skill):353 and (string,float):361, JobDemandHelper.GetIdealNumberOfDemands:124, JobDemandHelper.GetRandomHoursPerWeekDemandForSkill:142, RecruitmentAgencyDialog.OnRecruitmentSettingsSet:158, RecruitmentSettings.SelectSkill:126, HeadhunterPlan.GetWageRangeForSkill:74, HeadhunterPlan.CheckForRecruiting:108, HeadhunterPlan.GetRandomDemandsForCandidate:138. (Belt-and-braces — with a valid SkillData registered these do not fire, but registration is per-load and fragile.)
    3. Add the skill name to RecruitmentAgencySettings.availableEmployeeSkills (all recruitment-agency buildings) AND to the BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills of whatever business type the role is hired "under" (retail store type for Filiaalmanager/Team Leader, or the HQ business type if modelled like the Purchasing Agent). BusinessTypeHelper already keeps a ModBusinessTypes dict and BAModAPI.ModdingAPI exposes RegisterModBusinessType (BAModAPI/ModdingAPI.cs:10) / RegisterModVehicleType — but there is NO RegisterModSkill and no API to append to an existing BusinessType's employeePrimarySkills, so this is Harmony/reflection on the loaded asset.
    4. Provide a localization entry for the skill-name key (used as skillKey.GetLocalization() in RecruitmentCampaign.FinishCampaign:85, RecruitmentCampaignsList:41, dialog messages).
  Note the Purchasing Agent is recruited exactly this way: UI.Smartphone.Apps.BizMan/PurchasingAgentsPlanList.cs only ASSIGNS already-hired ba:skill_purchasingagent employees (filtered by assignedAddress == HQ + HasSkill + IsAssignedToAnyWorkShift, :111) to ImportPartnership plans — it has no recruit button. So "hired at the same place as the Purchasing Agent" == the Recruitment Agency campaign with the HQ business selected (and/or the Headhunter), which means ba:skill_purchasingagent is already present in the HQ BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills and in agency availableEmployeeSkills; a custom HQ role would need the same two entries.

feasibility: needs Harmony — Recruitment Agency: SkillHelper.Skills injection (reflection or Harmony postfix on SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded, re-run every save load) + guards on the ~9 unguarded SkillHelper.GetData(...) call sites + mutate RecruitmentAgencySettings.availableEmployeeSkills and BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills post-load (or Harmony-patch RecruitmentSettings.OnEnable/SelectBusiness/SelectSkill). Headhunter path: the skill LISTING is native once the skill is in SkillHelper (HeadhuntersRecruitingTab.SetUpSkillsToRecruitArray reads SkillHelper.AllSkillNames), but still needs the SkillData + the same GetData guards. No asset bundle strictly required (SkillData can be ScriptableObject.CreateInstance'd at runtime); an icon sprite for icon28 would want a bundle.
openQuestions: TaggedScriptableObject (SkillData's base) is not in this decomp dump — confirm the exact tag-storage field and that BuildTagCache() alone is enough after setting tags on a runtime-created SkillData, and which concrete TagRef.Skilltag values a Store-Manager/Team-Leader skill should carry (canhavejobdemands, hashoursperweekdemand vs forcefulltime, plus any icon/localization tags).

Does the save serializer (SaveGameSerializationHelper / DeserializeBinary/Json) use a fixed polymorphic type table for EmployeeInstance subclasses? If so a custom 'Filiaalmanager' EmployeeInstance subclass cannot be deserialized and the role must stay a base EmployeeInstance identified purely by its skill string (supervision logic driven from GlobalEvents.onNewHour/onNewDay, matching the existing mod design).

Exact BusinessType(s) that currently list ba:skill_purchasingagent / ba:skill_hrmanager / etc. in employeePrimarySkills (the HQ business type name) and whether every recruitment-agency building shares one RecruitmentAgencySettings asset or has per-building copies — determines how many assets the mod must patch and whether a single Harmony postfix covers them.

Whether AddressableLoader also re-runs on city change / HQ purchase (not just save load) — affects how often SkillHelper.Skills, BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills and RecruitmentAgencySettings.availableEmployeeSkills must be re-patched.
